title: Nightwatch
paragraphs: A documentary-style police series built from real field recordings as reporter Donn Reed accompanies Culver City police officers on night patrol.

CBS sustaining actuality/documentary series using authentic Culver City police field recordings rather than actors or scripts. The frozen GRH snapshot contains the audition plus 45 numbered broadcasts through program 49; four numbered slots inside 1-49 and programs 50-52 are absent.
GRH documents the program through CBS sustaining run (April 5, 1954 to April 21, 1955) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Donn Reed (performer on 46 recordings), Sterling Tracy (producer on 43 recordings, director on 29 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Jim Headlock (producer on 43 recordings and performer on 1 recording), W. N. Hildebrand (performer on 38 recordings), Ron Perkins (technical advisor on 35 recordings), W. L. Hildebrand (performer on 4 recordings), and Evelyn Bigsby (performer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include police patrol and law enforcement work, authentic field recording and actuality radio, juvenile incidents and child welfare, domestic conflict and family crisis, burglary, theft and property crime, and suicide and self-harm calls.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Early network actuality and reality-style radio, Portable tape recording in field journalism, CBS sustaining documentary programming, and Mid-1950s Culver City police actuality.
